agentContributions.notes: This is a novel story — the codebase has zero Live Preview integration. The project uses Next.js Pages Router (src/pages/_app.tsx), NOT App Router. The Contentstack Live Preview SDK docs explicitly state support only for Next.js CSR (App Router), creating a framework mismatch. However, the contentstack SDK v3.x itself supports live_preview config in Stack options independently of the separate @contentstack/live-preview-sdk package. The attachment points are: (1) src/services/contentstack.ts options/Stack for server-side draft fetching, (2) src/context/ContentstackContext.ts + src/pages/_app.tsx ContentstackContext.Provider for client-side content propagation, (3) src/hooks/useContent.ts as the consumer bridge, (4) src/constants/contentstack.ts contentstackConfig must be reused for preview queries. The ContentstackContext.Provider currently receives static content from pageProps — Live Preview requires this context value to be updatable when draft entries change. No @contentstack/live-preview-sdk dependency exists yet.

Openspec provided empty acceptanceCriteria with detailed architectural notes. I built the full AC list from scratch, grounded in actual codebase analysis. Key observations from reading the files: (1) Stack is initialized in contentstack.ts with options containing api_key, delivery_token, environment, branch — no live_preview key exists yet. (2) ContentstackContext is a simple createContext with no setter — value is static from pageProps via _app.tsx's ContentstackContext.Provider value={content}. Making it reactive is the core challenge. (3) useContent hook reads from context via useContext — no update mechanism. (4) contentstackConfig maps each ContentTypes enum value to referenceFieldPath/jsonRtePath/only/except — these must be reused for preview queries. (5) pageService uses getEntry, getSingleEntry, getSingletonEntry, findSingletonEntry — all four paths need draft support. (6) pageSpecificData (e.g., Homepage's station_order, SchedulesPage's stationHub) is fetched separately from the primary page entry — this creates a staleness risk during Live Preview. (7) Zero existing live_preview references anywhere in the codebase confirms this is fully greenfield for this feature. File contents were read and verified for all 6 core files in the upexpress codeline.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes:
Both agents added meaningful, non-overlapping value. Openspec correctly identified this as a greenfield feature (zero Live Preview integration exists), flagged the Pages Router vs. App Router mismatch with the vendor's @contentstack/live-preview-sdk docs, and named the four core attachment points (contentstack.ts options/Stack, ContentstackContext, useContent, contentstackConfig). Speckit independently read the actual source files and discovered concrete implementation constraints Openspec did not: ContentstackContext has no setter (value is static from pageProps), useContent has no update mechanism, pageService has four distinct fetch paths (getEntry, getSingleEntry, getSingletonEntry, findSingletonEntry) all needing draft support, and pageSpecificData creates a staleness risk during Live Preview. These findings are complementary and neither agent duplicated the other's work.

Manifest evidence is clean for the working codeline (upexpress): all 9 declared paths confirmed EXISTS. The per-codeline resolution shows gotransit and metrolinx have unresolved mock files (ContentstackAccordion/content.mock.ts, ContentstackColorComponent/content.mock.ts), but those are test-fixture files not referenced in fixSiteAnalysis — the four fix sites (contentstack.ts, pageService.ts, useContent.ts, contentstackConfig) all resolve to exact matches across all three codelines. No missing_manifest_path.

Verification criteria are observable: all three describe what the rendered page displays (draft content, updated content, published content) — directly testable by a human or automated check. The guard-vocabulary blacklist correctly flags internal terms like 'field values' and 'draft entry' that appear in the ticket's own immutable criteria, but on a brownfield ticket this is expected and not a defect.

Plan alignment is aligned: the detective's plan named investigating Stack initialization, useContent, preview config, and package.json — the fixSiteAnalysis covers contentstack.ts (options/Stack), pageService.ts (getEntry), useContent.ts, and contentstackConfig. Shared terms (contentstack, usecontent, preview) confirm alignment with no unexplained pivot.

The one substantive risk is the framework mismatch: vendor docs restrict @contentstack/live-preview-sdk to Next.js App Router, but this project uses Pages Router. Both agents identified this and the fixSiteAnalysis proposes using the SDK v3.x built-in live_preview config in Stack options rather than the separate live-preview-sdk package — a plausible and well-reasoned workaround, but unverified against Contentstack's actual v3.x capabilities. This is an ordinary open question a competent writer resolves during implementation, not a concrete defect in the spec.
